raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through as I sit here figuring out this year's plan.

---

I got 9 mu total. Six of them I keep in wheat-maize like always — that's the food for the family, seven mouths to feed and grain in the shed means we don't worry. The other three mu I put in cotton for cash. That's how my father did it, that's how I've done it for thirty years. No reason to change.

**Wheat (6 mu, already in the ground since October):** Planted Jimai variety, same as last year, neighbor Old Wang uses it too and his yields are decent. I put down about 2 bags of compound 15-15-15 per mu before planting, that's 40 kg — the base. Come March when it's jointing I'll topdress one bag of urea per mu, maybe 20 kg. If it looks yellow I'll add more, if it looks good I save the money. Irrigate after the Spring Festival when it turns green, then again at jointing, then once at grain filling if no rain. Three times usually, costs me maybe 30 yuan each time for the pump. Harvest early June. Hope for 400 kg/mu — last year I got 420, year before 380, depends on the weather.

**Maize (6 mu, goes in right after wheat in June):** Xianyu variety hybrid seed, I buy fresh every year, can't save hybrid seed. Right after wheat harvest I hire the neighbor's rotary tiller for 30 yuan/mu and plant within three-four days — window is tight. Put one-and-a-half bags compound per mu as base, topdress urea at big trumpet stage, maybe 15 kg. Irrigate once or twice if July-August is dry. Harvest end of September, expect around 450 kg/mu.

**Cotton (3 mu):** Plant end of April when soil warms. I keep my own seed from good plants but buy some fresh too. Cotton's more work — need to spray for bollworm three-four times through summer, that's where family labor comes in. My wife and the older kids help with picking in September and October, several pickings. Fertilizer lighter than grain, about one bag compound per mu base plus topdress at squaring. Expect maybe 250 kg lint per mu, selling price has been okay lately, that's why I keep it.

Money's tight with seven people at home. I try not to overspend on fertilizer but I won't cut it too much either — one bad year hurts worse than any savings. Family does almost all the work. Maybe hire a little help for cotton picking if the younger ones can't keep up.
